reason: The closure holds, and I re-verified it myself. (1) The numbers in r4_headscale_out.json match the finding exactly. On both embryos the mean distance to GT is lowest at s = 0.75-1.0 (44b6_nox 1.3006 at s = 1.0; 6bba_nox 1.5767 / 1.5769 at s = 1.0 / 0.75). s = 1.33 is +1.7% / +2.6% worse, and the 4 um re-match count falls steadily for s > 0.75 on both. The full sets, which keep the 20 probable x138 stems, give the same ordering, so the guessed exclusion list does not drive the result. (2) s = 1 in the desk script is exactly production. The exp58 notebook cell 4 applies bounded(head,(x-mean)/scale)/SPACING with no extra factor, so the 's075' naming does not hide a 1/0.75 rescale. (3) Any in-sample leakage of the public head onto the train videos would pull the optimum TOWARD s = 1. Out of sample, the optimum is therefore if anything <= 1, which strengthens the case against s > 1. (4) The pre-registered T12 gate (s_opt >= 1.25 and >= 4% on both embryos) fails decisively. In addition, s > 1 would trip the kernel's 2.00001 um RuntimeError guard, so the change would not even be fail-soft without editing the guard. (5) The adjacent 'shrink to s = 0.75' is not a hidden win. It gains +0.1% m4, the mean distance is mixed (worse on 44b6), and it would be a knob ladder after the new-mechanism cutoff. It stays closed too. No value or feasibility objection remains against closing.
